topic: TB-500 versus full-length Thymosin beta-4 nomenclature
whyItMatters: Protocol identity can be wrong if the names are treated as interchangeable.
currentSourceSignal: Practitioner sources use overlapping terminology without distinguishing the molecules.
neededVerification: Primary chemistry, sequence and product-definition sources.

whyItMatters: Practitioner sources differ on oral, subcutaneous, and local versus systemic approaches.
currentSourceSignal: LaValle, Hack Smith and Seeds describe different practical approaches.
neededVerification: Human evidence first; preclinical routes recorded separately; formulation-specific evidence required.

whyItMatters: Investigational trial regimens must not be replaced by community schedules.
currentSourceSignal: Practitioner and quick-reference materials contain practical protocol framing.
neededVerification: Clinical trial publications and registry records.

whyItMatters: Approved labelling and trial evidence must outrank quick-reference schedules.
neededVerification: Current approved labels and pivotal trial publications.

whyItMatters: Bioavailability is molecule- and formulation-specific; route-level generalisations are misleading.
currentSourceSignal: Broad route classes are discussed without molecule-specific qualification.

whyItMatters: Temperature and stability claims are frequently repeated without formulation-specific data.
currentSourceSignal: Practitioner material contains storage guidance of unclear origin.
neededVerification: Product- and formulation-specific stability studies and official labelling where available.

whyItMatters: Needed for credible shipping and receiving guidance.
currentSourceSignal: The current library has limited direct transport qualification evidence.
neededVerification: ICH stability guidance, good distribution practice, and formulation-specific excursion data.

whyItMatters: A high HPLC purity number is frequently mistaken for complete quality proof.
currentSourceSignal: Grant separates the roles of HPLC and mass spectrometry clearly.

topic: Sterility and endotoxin versus chemical purity
whyItMatters: A chemically pure sample is not automatically sterile or low in endotoxin.
currentSourceSignal: Current academic chemistry sources do not cover finished injectable release fully.

whyItMatters: Requires a factual, non-nationalistic explanation of global pharmaceutical supply chains.
currentSourceSignal: Current practitioner sources are not sufficient.
neededVerification: Current regulator and industry manufacturing disclosures.

whyItMatters: Requires a precise explanation of what a GMP system does and does not establish.
currentSourceSignal: Broader pharmaceutical texts in the library are partial copies.

topic: Strong anecdotal clinical claims in practitioner sources
whyItMatters: Case reports or author experience must not be presented as established outcomes.
currentSourceSignal: Several practitioner sources contain strongly worded clinical claims.
neededVerification: Trace the cited studies and separate anecdote from clinical evidence.

topic: SRC-011 replacement: Fields, Peptide Characterization and Application Protocols
whyItMatters: SRC-011 is a core source for the analytical chemistry the quality section rests on. The attribution question is resolved; the held copy is still unusable.
currentSourceSignal: Resolved as to identity. Front-matter inspection confirms Gregg B. Fields (ed.), Methods in Molecular Biology vol. 386, Humana Press, 2007, ISBN 978-1-58829-550-7. The Scribd wrapper page naming Colin T. Mant refers to the author of Chapter 1. The held copy remains unusable: 96 of roughly 500 pages, with filler after the opening of Chapter 1.
neededVerification: Obtain a complete verified copy. Identity no longer in question.

topic: Source integrity: five held files are not the works they claim to be
whyItMatters: An aggregator cover page carrying the correct title and ISBN, followed by unrelated text, is indistinguishable from a real copy in a file listing. Three of these were recorded as "genuine content after promotional pages", which would have allowed them to be cited.
currentSourceSignal: Audit on 2026-09-11 opened every file, hashed it, counted its pages and read its front matter. SRC-008, SRC-009, SRC-010, SRC-014 and SRC-015 carry 3-6% peptide-domain vocabulary across their pages, concentrated in the wrapper; their bodies are climate policy, Hume scholarship, fiction in three languages, African Union politics and project management. SRC-011 holds authentic Humana front matter and the opening of Chapter 1, then filler. SRC-013 is a two-page contents listing. SRC-001 to SRC-007 and SRC-012 are confirmed complete.
neededVerification: Obtain clean copies of the five decoys plus SRC-011 and SRC-013. Until then all seven are marked replace and are non-citable, which the publish gates enforce.

topic: The quality section rests on a single analytical source
whyItMatters: After the integrity audit, SRC-006 (Grant, Synthetic Peptides, 2nd ed., OUP 2002) is the only complete analytical reference held. It is authoritative on chromatographic principles, which have not changed, but it is twenty-plus years old and says nothing about current compendial method requirements or regulatory expectations. A quality section resting on one source of one age is fragile: if that source is ever downgraded, everything built on it is withdrawn at once.
currentSourceSignal: SRC-011 and SRC-013, the other analytical and formulation references, are both unusable. No compendial or regulatory source is in the register at all.
neededVerification: Add at least one current compendial or regulatory analytical source, and one modern analytical text, before the quality section is extended beyond chromatographic principles.
